public_rationale: The evidence supports sensitivity to wording. It does not establish the additional claim that quirks of training data explain apparent commonsense competence. Calling correct answers an illusion also requires an interpretation beyond measuring errors. The full proposition therefore remains unresolved, although its weaker claim about imperfect robustness has support.
limitations: Several evaluated models have undisclosed training corpora.
The selected study changes instructions, not training data.
Adversarial vulnerability does not show that all successful reasoning is superficial.

our_interpretation: Read illusion behaviorally: apparently competent answers do not establish robust commonsense generalization. This is not a claim about consciousness.
Retain both stated dependencies: question wording and training-data composition or patterns. Wording sensitivity alone does not settle the full claim.
Evidence of dependence on training data must go beyond the trivial fact that models are trained on data.
Use 2023 through publication as the contemporary evaluation period; the source names no narrower period or reporting cycle.
criteria.support_condition: Contemporary evaluations demonstrate apparently successful commonsense performance that is unreliable under equivalent wording and establish a relevant dependence on training-data composition or artifacts.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Controlled evaluations establish robust commonsense generalization across equivalent wording and relevant training-distribution changes, undermining the proposed explanation of apparent competence.
